label: DRC v. Rwanda ICJ case status
delta: Aug 6, 2026: DRC memorial due Oct 4, 2027; Rwanda counter-memorial due Dec 4, 2028
deltaNote: ICJ set the merits-phase timetable Aug 6, 2026; oral hearings would begin in early 2029 with judgment roughly six months later if the schedule holds — a multi-year process despite the June admissibility ruling.

label: Washington Accords status
delta: First EJVM+ mission deployed to Minembwe Aug 24; DRC and M23 traded fresh atrocity accusations same day
deltaNote: DRC and M23 agreed a sequenced roadmap after Aug 17-21 Geneva talks; the first EJVM+ verification mission then deployed to Minembwe on Aug 24, but DRC accused M23 of killing 300+ people in June-July and M23 accused government forces of an artillery attack near Minembwe — signalling the mechanism has yet to reduce mutual distrust. FDLR disarmament remains the unresolved core DRC-Rwanda obligation.

label: Doha comprehensive peace deal target
contestNote: An Aug 22, 2026 roadmap set sequenced negotiation steps, but M23 has made no firm disarmament commitments and fighting widened across Fizi, Minembwe, Kalehe, Masisi and Walungu even as the roadmap was signed

label: People needing humanitarian aid, 2026
deltaNote: Insecurity, gender-based violence and cholera outbreaks compound the crisis

label: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak deaths
contestNote: Congolese health experts say the true toll may be up to three times higher than the 6,342 confirmed cases, since the outbreak — declared May 15, 2026 in Ituri — spread undetected for weeks beforehand.
delta: 6,342 confirmed cases, 770 hospitalized in isolation, as of the Sept 3, 2026 report (data through Sept 2)
deltaNote: 92 new confirmed cases and 33 new deaths since the Sept 2 report, concentrated in Ituri (60), North Kivu (25), Haut-Uele (5) and Tshopo (2). Now DRC's largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak on record, surpassing the 2018-2020 outbreak's 3,317 cases, and the second-largest globally — UN relief chief Tom Fletcher warned Sept 1 the response faces a $1.1B funding gap while 'the virus is moving faster.' Ituri remains hardest hit with 5,164 cases/2,342 deaths across 28 of 36 health zones; North Kivu has 913 cases/614 deaths across 15 of 34 zones.
